description:
**Divergence**: MetadataBackend::get_metadata_changes default (crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/backend.rs:201) silently drops the `filterRelatedType` and `filterMetadataType` args, delegating to get_changes. The metadata.rs handler (crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/metadata.rs:175-215) post-filters `created` and `updated` by re-fetching each id and checking the related-type / metadata-type, but does NOT post-filter `destroyed` (the objects are gone — you cannot re-fetch them to check their type).

**Caller-observable effect**: a client requesting `Metadata/changes` with `filterRelatedType: "Email"` against a backend that ships the default impl will receive correctly-filtered `created` and `updated` arrays but a `destroyed` array containing ids for every related type. draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01 §3.3 requires the filter to apply to all three.

**Sibling positions** (cross-trait alignment for filter-args-aware /changes /query defaults):
- jmap-calendars-server `query_calendar_events` (line 529) and `get_calendar_events` (line 483) — silently drop §5.7 / §5.11 extras with NO handler compensation (see bd:JMAP-ic0j.26).
- jmap-metadata-server (this bead) — silently drops with PARTIAL handler compensation, acknowledged in rustdoc.
- jmap-filenode-server `query_subtree` (line 363) — REFERENCE PATTERN: rustdoc explicitly cites workspace 'no silent-drop' policy from AGENTS.md, propagates errors instead of partial results.

**The workspace has three different patterns for the same problem**. Either metadata's documented partial-compliance is the convention (and calendars should adopt it) or filenode's no-silent-drop is the convention (and both metadata and calendars should adopt it). Status quo is incoherent.

**Recommendation options**:
(a) Drop the default; require backends to honor the filter args (filenode pattern). Strictest, blocks the partial-compliance escape hatch.
(b) Keep the default + handler post-filter for created/updated, but extend the post-filter to destroyed by maintaining a side-table of (id, relatedType, metadataType) for recently-destroyed ids in the reference impl. Workable but adds storage.
(c) Document the partial-compliance status as a permanent kit limitation in the capability advertising surface (e.g. a flag on MetadataCapability that says 'destroyed array is unfiltered when filterRelatedType set'). Most honest but spec doesn't have a slot for it.

**Cross-references**: bd:JMAP-ic0j.26 (calendars-server, broader pattern). This bead specifically covers the metadata-server instance + the workspace-wide pattern-selection question.
title: metadata-server: MetadataBackend::get_metadata_changes default + handler partial-compensation leaves 'destroyed' array unfiltered (draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01 §3.3 partial violation)
